fails the query.**

- generator SHA-256: `b5644546065489def636ca0818f22ae8d311b027ccaa1e07010aa0ef45ce5f6b`;
- executed rule hash: `c7287233192c`; rule-text SHA-256: `561373e4ebc55b6e5e9bcec8d506b63cdb44ef71467ac398025322159a876415`;
- seed 9, omitted difficulty, sample indices 0..3;
- all four inputs pass the target's `self_check`.

Samples 0, 1, and 2 each contain one color-2 marker, so the true rule selects the
outermost frame. The rival **always select the outermost frame** therefore matches
all three demonstrations exactly. Sample 3 contains two markers and must select
frame index 1; the rival differs from the exact Racket output in 117 cells.

The rival was constructed without a Python rule mirror: remove all but one
marker, execute the exact canonical Racket rule, then restore the original
outside-frame marker cells. This isolates only the selector shortcut.

puts at least two selector values in every demonstration set and refutes the
rivals under supported query rotations. No source fix was made in this audit.
